additional_findings.issue: Module docstring at mattel_news_source.py:10-17 contains the literal string `__NEXT_DATA__` in the historical migration-note paragraph. The audit checklist literally says 'No leftover comments referencing __NEXT_DATA__'. While this is clearly intentional historical documentation (not stale leftover code), a strict reading of the checklist could call it out.
additional_findings.fix: Either (a) keep as-is and rely on this audit's interpretation (recommended — the migration context is genuinely useful for future maintainers), or (b) rephrase to 'the legacy embedded-JSON island disappeared' without naming it. Low-stakes call, leaving to operator/team preference.

additional_findings.issue: `_resolve_body_html` calls `re.compile` once per article fetch (mattel_news_source.py:316-318). The pattern depends on a runtime `row_id` so a direct module-level compile is not possible, but the row_id can equally be matched via a generic module-level pattern `re.compile(r'(?:^|[^0-9])(\d+):T([0-9a-fA-F]+),')` and then the matched group compared to `row_id` in Python. Avoids per-fetch regex compilation.
additional_findings.fix: Optional refactor: hoist a generic row-marker regex to module scope, scan with `finditer`, filter for `m.group(1) == row_id`. Performance gain is small (article fetch is dominated by HTTP); main benefit is consistency with `_FLIGHT_PUSH_RE` placement and clearer audit story (single module-level regex constant).

additional_findings.issue: `_extract_entries` (mattel_news_source.py:243-249) is a one-line wrapper around `_extract_listing_entries`. The comment explains it exists for Decision 3 import-stability. This is fine as-is; just noting that future readers may wonder why two names exist for the same operation. The docstring already covers it.
additional_findings.fix: No change needed — documented intent is clear. Could optionally add a `# noqa` or move the docstring's Decision-3 reference closer to the def. Low priority.

summary: All 7 architectural Decisions (1–7) are honored end-to-end, the fail-soft ES1–ES10 notifier matrix is correctly implemented (including the no-notifier ES9c body-empty path), preserved helper names + signatures (`_is_hotwheels`, `_build_entry`, `_extract_entries`, `_notify`) match code-research §11.3, the shared `tests/fixtures/mattel_flight_builder.py` module exposes the API per §11.4 with placeholder defaults, `_FLIGHT_PUSH_RE` is module-level, no `requests.Session()` constructor exists, and the anti-drift smoke tests are correctly `pytest.skip`-guarded on `/tmp/mattel_*.html`. Three minor findings (one documentation-hygiene call on the migration-note docstring, one performance/style suggestion to hoist `_resolve_body_html`'s regex, one optional clarity note on the `_extract_entries` wrapper) — all non-blocking. Verdict: approved.
